before.name: Samaria (city)
before.note: The northern kingdom's capital city, the hill of Samaria founded by Omri, besieged and fallen as described in Kings, Chronicles, Amos and Micah, and the city where Philip preaches in Acts; distinct from the wider region and from Sychar.

stages.text: Samaria: a broad, steep hill rising alone out of the central hill country, its slopes terraced with olive and vine. Walls of dressed limestone ring the crown, with a gate opening onto an open place by the entrance. Within stand a royal palace of cut stone and cedar beams, a house of Baal with an altar, and a pool at the foot of the hill.

stages.text: Samaria: a region of central hill country with rounded limestone ridges and terraced olive groves on the slopes, dry grass between stony fields, and valleys of terebinth and fig. Villages of plastered mud-brick and rough fieldstone houses with flat roofs cluster near springs and wells; a walled city stands on a hill with a stone gate and watchtowers, and a road runs through the valleys toward Galilee and Jerusalem.
